currentState.summary: Ordinary gpux Div stickies resolve independently in Window against the nearest per-axis scroll context and paint through the positioned scene lane. RayX VirtualStickyItems stores sorted StickyRow candidates and a copied active stack at every candidate. ListViewState and TreeViewState rebuild one cached sticky policy outside the scroll path and render sticky metadata on the virtual row root wrapper. gpux List and UniformList retain offscreen candidates through separate flat-index and explicit-level APIs and derive active stacks locally.

decisions.title: Use one neutral relation with contiguous keyed runs
decisions.decision: Introduce a gpux-owned StickyStacking relation with mutually exclusive Level(u16) and StackId(ElementId) modes. Build ordered relation indexes in linear memory. Equal adjacent StackId values append to a run; every different identifier starts a new root and drops the prior chain; A-B-A creates three runs.
decisions.rationale: The existing level algorithm already defines parent replacement. A keyed run is the same relation with depth derived from adjacent equality, while explicit levels remain available for real hierarchy. Centralizing the relation prevents four subtly different stack algorithms.

evidence.reason: Existing level stack demonstrates replacement and cumulative offsets.

provenance.userDecision: Use an identical identifier to make sticky elements stack like parent-child stickies.

alternativesRejected.reason: A-B-A would resurrect obsolete headers and violate document-order section replacement.

alternativesRejected.reason: It preserves the manual hierarchy calculation the feature is intended to remove.

decisions.title: Plan ordinary keyed stickies before committing final bounds
decisions.decision: Extend the gpux positioned lifecycle with a frame-local discovery and resolution phase for keyed ordinary sticky candidates. Scope candidate registries by the nearest scroll context and edge, compute the active keyed plan after candidate layout bounds and group boundaries are known, then let Div commit the resolved visual bounds through the existing sticky bounds, mask, hitbox, child, callback, and positioned paint path.
decisions.rationale: A sequential accumulator cannot remove old descendant lanes when a later different-key root becomes active. Ordinary keyed replacement requires later candidate knowledge, while the existing Div lifecycle must remain the only owner of final visual effects.

evidence.reason: Existing Window positioning is the correct framework boundary.
Prior architecture decision places layout-affecting positioned behavior in GPUI.

decisions.title: Extend StickyRow and replace copied virtual stacks
decisions.decision: Add StickyRow::stack_id(id) and store the canonical StickyStacking relation. Replace VirtualStickyItems.active_stack_indices with the shared linear-memory relation index. Preserve sticky_policy evaluation during projection rebuilds and preserve the existing conditional root wrapper for geometry, styling, callbacks, identity, semantics, and interaction.
decisions.rationale: Virtual layers already have the right single-source policy and root wrapper. Only relation metadata and the candidate index need to change; creating another policy or wrapper would duplicate ownership.

decisions.title: Converge low-level list candidates on structured metadata
decisions.decision: Replace the internal flat and level-only candidate storage in ListState and UniformList with one structured gpux sticky candidate type containing item index and StickyStacking relation. Keep one flat level-zero convenience entry point only where it remains a direct mapping, provide one structured configuration surface for level or key, and remove superseded parallel APIs and row-local keyed depth calculations in the same change.
decisions.rationale: Low-level lists must retain offscreen candidates, so row-local div metadata is insufficient. A structured candidate type reuses the canonical relation without importing RayX StickyRow or adding a third stack-key vector.

evidence.reason: ListState already requires collection-level hierarchy metadata.
